title: Is “could not load” an empty state or an error state?
context: EmptyState has tone="error" in the code, and its Usage, Behavior and Error variant use it with Retry. A separate Error state page also exists.

current.text: Content that could not load: tone="error" names the problem and gives the one action that recovers (Retry)
…name the problem and give the one action that recovers (Retry); it is announced as an alert. An error in one field stays at the field.
"error" (the content could not load: the title names the problem, the action recovers; announced as an alert, the icon in the danger color)

current.text: EmptyState is what a region shows when it has nothing to show: nothing yet, no results, or content that could not load. It says what the place is for and gives the one action that follows, as a whole view or a line inside a list.

title: Should the Snackbar overview mention that danger toasts stay?
context: The overview now mentions it, matching the code.

current.text: A snackbar (Material’s name) is the Plenix toast: a short message about what just happened, at the edge of the window, that leaves on its own (a danger toast stays until dismissed); useToast().show(message, { tone }) shows it, and every toast has Dismiss.
The danger tone: a danger start border and the alert icon. It stays until dismissed unless a `duration` is given.

recommendation: A. A message that can vanish before people reach it fails WCAG 2.2.1; Carbon keeps error toasts until dismissed.

title: Should Health and Severity use the status badge instead of a dot?
context: Your rule: statuses are a badge with an icon. Health’s overview already says so, but its written sections still describe StatusDot; Severity still says StatusDot.

current.text: The health of a service or a sync is a status badge with its icon: success for working, waiting for slow or partial, negative for down. Status dot remains only for a person’s availability.
Marks a state (active, paused, priority) with a small tone dot. It is a quick visual cue next to a status in words.
Severity is a StatusDot in the tone of the level, with the level in words: info for a note, warning for something to check, danger for something broken. Lists sorted by severity put danger first.
